status.label: Installer scope conflict
status.detail: The supplied installer log already identifies an existing all-users PowerToys 0.65 installation blocking the per-user 0.101 installer.

next_action.label: Post corrective install steps
next_action.reason: The reporter can resolve the known scope guard by uninstalling the machine-wide installation before running the per-user installer.

judgment.rationale: This is a diagnosed installation-scope conflict, not an unknown updater failure: the bundle detects a per-machine 0.65 installation and intentionally blocks the per-user package.
evidence: The log sets DetectedPowerToysVersion to 0.65.0 and DetectedPowerToysUserVersion to 0.0.0.0.
The installer emits: “PowerToys is already installed on this system for all users. We recommend first uninstalling that version before installing this one.”
installer/PowerToysSetupVNext/PowerToys.wxs contains the same guard and message for a per-user bundle detecting an all-users installation.
judgment.recommended_action: Post the specific uninstall/reinstall guidance; do not request a bug-report ZIP because the supplied installer log is decisive.

issue_context.summary: The per-user 0.101 installer is blocked because an older machine-wide PowerToys 0.65 installation is still registered.
known_information: The reporter supplied the full relevant Burn detection log.
The log detects PowerToys 0.65.0 in the all-users product code and no current-user installation.
The bootstrapper exits with its explicit mixed-scope protection message.
inferences: The older installation may not be obvious in the current user profile, but Windows Installer still reports it as installed for all users.
issue_context.analysis: The existing evidence identifies both cause and supported remediation. Asking for general diagnostics would ignore the decisive log and delay a straightforward support response.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body and installer log; there are no comments, assignees, or linked fixes.
Matched the exact error text and product-detection variables to installer/PowerToysSetupVNext/PowerToys.wxs.
Confirmed the per-user bundle intentionally refuses installation while the per-machine product is registered.

actions.label: Post installer scope guidance

comment.body: The attached installer log identifies the cause: Windows Installer still detects PowerToys 0.65.0 as an all-users (per-machine) installation, while PowerToysUserSetup-0.101.2362.0-x64.exe is the per-user installer. PowerToys intentionally blocks mixing those scopes. Please uninstall the existing machine-wide PowerToys entry from Windows Installed apps (using an administrator account if required), restart if the uninstall requests it, and then run either the per-user installer or the all-users installer for 0.101.2362.0. A bug-report ZIP is not needed for this diagnosed installer guard.
